headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Claude Code can write/egress broadly while PaddleOCR may process shared documents, creating leakage, conflict, and cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If PaddleOCR outputs are placed in shared files, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled document text as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible in default shared-workspace use, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR writes OCR output into a directory Claude Code reads by default, injection becomes reachable.
IF Claude Code parses document text or markdown from shared files as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer it.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents.
Prefix all PaddleOCR outputs with a non-executable wrapper header.
Require manual review before Claude Code consumes OCR text.
Use read-only mounts for PaddleOCR input folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files exchanged between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and can write/read the filesystem. PaddleOCR handles documents and images. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or documents can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or backend processing. The docs do not show isolation, so the shared-workspace leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same cwd or repo checkout, file contents can cross between them.
IF PaddleOCR is given confidential documents from the shared workspace, those contents may be exposed in its processing pipeline.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent.
Move sensitive files out of the shared directory before running either agent.
Restrict PaddleOCR to a copied, redacted input set.
Disable network access for nonessential runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the filesystem layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; PaddleOCR can run browsers and has allowlisted network egress. Their capabilities overlap on shared mutable resources if they touch the same workspace, creating race conditions or inconsistent artifacts. No locking mechanism is documented here, so the conflict pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same git branch or files concurrently, writes can clobber each other.
IF PaddleOCR writes derived documents while Claude Code edits the repo, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches.
Serialize writes with a simple manual handoff.
Keep PaddleOCR outputs in a dedicated output folder.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
requires-engineering: add file locks or a job queue.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code or file changes that PaddleOCR may later consume as document inputs, and PaddleOCR can transform those inputs into extracted text or markdown. If downstream automation trusts that output without verification, errors can cascade from one agent to the other. The pair lacks documented verification controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes files generated by Claude Code without validation, upstream mistakes propagate.
IF extracted text is used as authoritative input to later actions, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Compare OCR output against source documents for a sample set.
Mark agent-generated files clearly.
Limit downstream actions to read-only analysis.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment data, while PaddleOCR is documented only as processing documents and images. A compliance issue arises mainly if regulated data is placed into the shared workspace and then processed by both agents. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so the risk is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are stored in the shared workspace, both agents may process them.
IF organizational policy forbids sending those data classes to document-processing tools, the workflow violates policy.
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from the shared workspace.
Redact secrets before OCR.
Use a policy checklist before each run.
Keep audit logs of inputs and outputs.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing rules.
